title: Best Speak App Alternatives August 2026
summary: August 2026 roundup of 7 Speak alternatives ranked by voice practice quality, language support, and cost per spoken rep.
body_markdown:
You open Speak, work through the lesson, do the drills, and feel like you're making progress. Then someone speaks to you off-script and your mind goes blank. That gap between structured practice and real conversation is exactly where Speak's design shows its limits. The seven alternatives below each take a different approach to closing it.


**TLDR:**


- Speak costs $17.99 USD per month and works well for beginners learning American English through structured curriculum, but its scripted conversational flow limits free-form speaking practice at B1 and above.
- Sticker price is the wrong comparison unit: a cheaper app used twice a week costs more per spoken rep than a pricier one used daily, so divide monthly cost by realistic session count before deciding.
- Loora covers English-for-work only, Praktika fits A2 to B1 structured learners, Talkpal offers 130+ languages in a text-first format, Duolingo builds habits but multiple-choice drills don't build spoken recall, and italki pairs human accountability with per-session pricing.
- ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor covering 60+ languages with cross-session memory, conversation-anchored SRS flashcards, a separate Shadowing mode for pronunciation, and background mode for commutes, at $20 to $29 per month for unlimited practice.


## What is Speak and how does it work?


Speak is an AI language app built around one idea: fluency comes from speaking out loud, not tapping matching pairs. The product follows a three-step loop. You learn phrases native speakers actually use through short video lessons, drill them until they come out without hesitation, then apply them in[open conversation with AI speaking practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/how-ai-speaking-practice-works/) .


The curriculum is the spine of the experience. Speak organizes learning into thematic units, and each unit mixes video-based tutor explanations, speaking drills that force repetition until the phrase becomes automatic, and freer conversational practice at the end. The app leans structured, which suits learners who want a clear path from lesson one forward.


### Supported languages


Speak covers 17 languages including Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, and Portuguese (full list on the App Store). The catalog is narrower than some competitors, but depth per language tends to be higher because each course is built around the same framework.


### How much is Speak app?


Verified 2026 pricing sits at roughly[$17.99 per month or $83.99 per year](https://speakshark.com/blog/speak-app-review-2026) . The annual plan works out to about $7 per month. Free-trial availability changes often, so check the live site before subscribing.


Speak fits beginner and lower-intermediate learners who want guided structure. Advanced learners looking for open-ended conversation volume often find the curriculum-first design more limiting than freeing, and[effective language learning techniques](https://www.issen.com/blog/most-effective-language-learning-techniques-ai/) tend to require more adaptive practice.


## Why consider Speak alternatives?


Speak has real strengths. The production quality is high, the video lessons are well-scripted, and the curriculum gives beginners a clear path from lesson one. For English learners in particular, Speak works as a curriculum-first product where produced video lessons set the agenda and AI conversation sits on top as the application layer. If you want structure and you are learning American English, it holds up.


The limitations show up once you push past that comfort zone.


- One accent. Speak's English coverage is American only. Learners preparing for work in London, Sydney, or a mixed international team have to look elsewhere for exposure to other varieties.
- Scripted conversational flow. The AI conversations lean on phrases from the current lesson, which keeps drills tight but leaves less room for the unpredictable, free-form speaking practice that builds real fluency.
- Opaque progression. You can practice a lot, but that is not the same as moving clearly from A2 to B1, per[Languavibe's 2026 review](https://languavibe.com/speak-review/) .
- Ceiling for advanced learners. Speak works best for beginners and lower-intermediate learners; its value at B2 and above depends heavily on how you use it.


If you need open-ended voice practice, multiple accents, cross-session memory, or support for switching between languages mid-sentence, Speak will feel narrow, and[AI apps for real conversations](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-apps-practicing-language-real-conversations/) cover that gap more directly. That is the gap the alternatives below cover.


## Best Speak alternatives in August 2026


### 1. ISSEN (best overall alternative)


ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor built around open-ended speaking practice. Conversations start within 30 seconds of opening the app, with no push-to-talk thanks to smart turn detection. Vocabulary you use in sessions flows into conversation-anchored SRS flashcards, and a separate[shadowing pronunciation technique](https://www.issen.com/blog/shadowing-pronunciation-technique/) mode handles pronunciation drills across accents like American, British, Australian, Argentinian, Mexican, and Castilian.


- What it does well: 60+ languages, multiple regional accents (Argentina, Mexico, Spain for Spanish; American, British, Australian for English), cross-session memory, background mode for walks and commutes, multilingual input including Spanglish, flat $20 to $29 USD per month.
- Where it falls short: not a fit for absolute beginners who want a rigid lesson path; no in-conversation pronunciation grading (that lives in Shadowing).


Bottom line: ISSEN delivers the daily speaking reps Speak is built around without the scripted-path ceiling.


### 2. Loora


Loora is an[AI spoken-English tutor built for adult professionals](https://oxfordenglishglobal.com/blog/loora-ai-review/) who want to sharpen how they sound at work, running interview and client-call simulations with real-time grammar and fluency feedback.


- What it does well: strong English-only depth for B1+ professionals, cross-device access (verify on live site), post-session written feedback (verify on live site).
- Where it falls short: Loora focuses solely on English. No smart turn detection, cross-session memory, conversation-anchored SRS, dedicated Shadowing mode, or background mode.


Bottom line: solid for English-for-work; anyone learning another language should look elsewhere.


### 3. Praktika


Praktika is a polished AI app built around animated avatars and structured paths, covering English, Arabic, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Thai, and Turkish.


- What it does well: avatar-guided structure and pronunciation feedback at roughly $8 per month billed annually (verify on the live site).
- Where it falls short: no smart turn detection, cross-session memory, conversation-anchored SRS, or dedicated Shadowing mode. The rigid path limits open-ended practice.


Bottom line: works for A2 to B1 learners building a foundation; less useful once you need unscripted output.


### 4. Talkpal


Talkpal is a[GPT-powered AI conversation tutor](https://toolchase.com/tool/talkpal/) that plays roles, debates, and corrects in real time.


- What it does well: more than 130 languages, with premium annual billing at $89.99 per year (verify on the live site).
- Where it falls short: text-first design, no smart turn detection, no cross-session memory, no conversation-anchored SRS, no dedicated Shadowing mode.


Bottom line: affordable breadth; weaker if voice fluency is your only goal.


### 5. Duolingo


Duolingo remains the gamified vocabulary and habit-formation benchmark, though[language learning apps for speaking](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-language-learning-apps-speaking/) serve different goals than habit streaks. Duolingo Max adds Roleplay and Explain My Answer across German, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese (verify current language scope on the live site), though sessions stay guided and predictable.


- What it does well: strong free tier, streak-driven habit formation, absolute-beginner accessibility.
- Where it falls short: Duolingo Max is annual-only (verify current pricing on the live site) and limited to a handful of languages. Multiple-choice drills do not build spoken recall.


Bottom line: a fine starting point; a poor daily speaking gym.


### 6. Babbel


Babbel offers structured grammar sequencing with speech recognition exercises across multiple languages, though[AI voice tutors for language learning](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-voice-tutors-language-learning/) are built for a different kind of output entirely.


- What it does well: explicit grammar progression, offline access, roughly $7 per month on annual billing (verify on the live site).
- Where it falls short: recognition-based exercises only, no open-ended voice conversation, no smart turn detection, cross-session memory, or conversation-anchored SRS.


Bottom line: good for grammar; not built for spontaneous speaking output.


### 7. italki


italki is a human tutor marketplace covering hundreds of languages. Per-session rates typically run from about $10 to $50+ USD per hour; verify on the live site.


- What it does well: human accountability, cultural nuance, targeted correction of fossilized errors.
- Where it falls short: per-session pricing makes daily reps expensive, scheduling friction blocks spontaneous practice, no AI session continuity.


Bottom line: The[AI vs. human tutor](https://www.issen.com/blog/ai-vs-human-tutor-language-speaking/) tradeoff is real: human tutors for weekly depth, ISSEN for daily volume.

### Reframing the price question


Sticker price is the wrong unit, especially when comparing[language learning apps with AI voice](https://www.issen.com/blog/ai-language-learning-apps-voice-practice/) against apps that rely on recognition drills. What matters is cost per spoken rep. If you practice five days a week for a month, that's roughly 20 sessions. At $17.99 per month, Speak works out to about $0.90 per session, but only if you actually use the scripted curriculum daily. A $7 annual Babbel plan looks cheaper until you notice you're getting recognition drills, not conversation. ISSEN at $24 per month across 20 sessions lands near $1.20 per open-ended voice conversation with cross-session memory and unlimited practice length. A single italki lesson can cost more than an entire month of any AI tutor. Divide, then decide.


## Why ISSEN is the best Speak alternative


Speak earns its polish. The video lessons are well-produced, the curriculum gives beginners a clear starting line, and the onboarding is one of the smoothest in the category. If you are learning American English from scratch and want a structured path, it holds up. The problem is that reaching conversational fluency requires extensive free-form speaking practice, and Speak's scripted, curriculum-tied model was not built to deliver that at daily volume.


ISSEN is architected the other way around. Voice is the primary interface. The tutor drives sessions instead of waiting for you to prompt it, adjusts vocabulary and pace inside a single turn, and remembers what you struggled with last time so the next session picks up where the last one ended. Sessions adapt to your accent target too, whether that is American, British, or Australian English, and the same applies across Spanish (Argentina, Mexico, Spain) and the other 55+ languages ISSEN supports. That real-time adaptive layer is what Speak cannot supply at scale, and that is where daily speaking reps actually compound, which is why[AI language tutors for real conversation](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-language-tutors-conversation-practice/) outperform scripted apps for fluency-focused learners.


Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes.


## Final thoughts on picking the best Speak alternative for your needs


The right app depends on what Speak is missing for you in particular. If the gap is accent variety, open-ended conversation, or cross-session memory, the alternatives above cover those areas in different ways. Price per month looks clean until you divide by actual sessions, and that number tells a more useful story. The comparison table above lays out where each app lands across the features that shape daily practice.[Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes](https://issen.com/) if you want to test open-ended, real-time voice practice before committing to a subscription. Sessions start in 30 seconds with no push-to-talk required, and the tutor remembers your conversation history from session one.


## FAQs


### Why do people look for Speak app alternatives?


Speak works well for beginners learning American English through a structured curriculum, but its scripted conversational format limits free-form speaking practice at higher levels. Learners at B1 and above often find the curriculum-tied AI conversations too predictable to build real spontaneous fluency, and the single-accent English coverage excludes anyone preparing for British, Australian, or internationally mixed environments.


### How much is the Speak app compared to other AI voice tutors?


Speak runs roughly $17.99 per month or $83.99 per year (about $7 per month annually) as of 2026, though free-trial availability fluctuates, so check the live site before subscribing. For comparison, ISSEN costs $20 to $29 USD per month with unlimited practice sessions, which works out to a lower cost per spoken rep for learners who practice five or more days a week.


### When should you consider switching from Speak to ISSEN?


The clearest signal is when the scripted lesson format starts to feel like a ceiling and not a guide, which typically happens around the B1 level. If you need open-ended voice conversation, cross-session memory, regional accent options beyond American English, or the ability to switch between languages mid-sentence, Speak's curriculum-first architecture will not supply those things at daily volume.


### What features should you focus on when comparing Speak alternatives for speaking practice?


Focus on three things: whether voice conversations are open-ended or scripted, whether the app remembers your previous sessions, and whether turn detection is automatic or push-to-talk. Smart turn detection, cross-session memory, and conversation-anchored vocabulary review are the structural features that separate tools built for daily speaking reps from tools that treat voice as an add-on to a lesson path.


### Can you use ISSEN alongside Speak instead of replacing it entirely?


Yes, and for some learners that pairing makes sense. Speak's structured video lessons work as a foundation for beginners building grammar and phrase patterns, while ISSEN supplies the open-ended, daily conversational reps that structured curricula cannot generate at scale. ISSEN is designed to complete a study stack, not replace every other resource in it.
